# Third-party notices

Margo Engine's own code is licensed under the Apache License 2.0 (`LICENSE` and `NOTICE`; every tarball ships both). This file lists everything else that
reaches users: npm packages our published packages depend on, third-party code shipped inside our tarballs, and the
assets the site and examples use. It covers all 112 published packages (109 in `packages/`
plus `create-margo`, `margo-convert` and `margo-convert-cad`). `node scripts/supply-chain.mjs --check` (in `npm run verify`, through
`tests/supply-chain.test.js`) fails when this file is stale, a dependency has no stated reason, a licence is outside
the allowed list, or a runtime dependency has an install script, a deprecation or a non-registry source.

## Runtime npm dependencies of published packages (direct and transitive)

98 of 112 packages have no third-party runtime dependency at all (internal `@margoengine/*` ranges only).
Versions are the ones in `package-lock.json`; users get whatever their own lockfile resolves inside our ranges.

| Package | Version (lock) | Licence | Kind | Used by | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `react` | 19.3.0 | MIT | optional peer | @margoengine/game, @margoengine/kit-react, @margoengine/machinery, @margoengine/react, @margoengine/ui, margoengine | React component bindings for the stage |
| `react-dom` | 19.3.0 | MIT | optional peer | @margoengine/kit-react, @margoengine/react, margoengine | React DOM root and portal rendering for scene and HTML components |
| `scheduler` | 0.28.0 | MIT | transitive (via react-dom) | @margoengine/kit-react | React DOM scheduling dependency |
| `web-ifc` | 0.0.78 | MPL-2.0 | optional peer | @margoengine/ifc, margoengine | IFC (BIM) parser; the app installs and initializes it, the package only reads its output |

None of them has an install script (`preinstall`/`install`/`postinstall`), a deprecation notice or a source other
than registry.npmjs.org with an integrity hash. Peers are installed by the app, not by us.

### Licence obligations and how they are met

- **Apache-2.0 (Draco, Basis, jxl-oxide under its Apache-2.0 option; no peers).** Redistribution must carry the licence text, keep the upstream
  notices and mark modified files. `@margoengine/decoders` ships `dist/LICENSE-Apache-2.0.txt` and
  `dist/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICE.md` (projects, sources, what changed); the modified `basis_transcoder.js` states the change
  in its first line. Neither upstream build ships a NOTICE file to carry forward. Rapier 3D (@dimforge/rapier3d-compat, Apache-2.0) is a root devDependency that comparison tests load; it is not redistributed.
  The vendored files are byte-identical to the official releases (checked 2026-10-24; `.gitattributes` keeps them
  binary so checkouts do not change line endings):
  - Draco 1.5.6 glTF decoder from https://www.gstatic.com/draco/versioned/decoders/1.5.6/:
    `draco_decoder_gltf.wasm` (sha256 `a680d927bed9cb864ddbd63521868891af2bfbe755092761b4837487618df8ac`) as
    `draco_decoder.wasm`, `draco_wasm_wrapper_gltf.js`
    (`8bb2952d2ba7d67e1414f8df819410cb0434a666be53f671fff75f68843d76f6`) as `draco_wasm_wrapper.js`.
  - Draco 1.5.6 full decoder, for point clouds, from the same folder (checked 2026-11-06): `draco_decoder.wasm` (sha256
    `c55a594e8ffd18426d36b27fea9618af3df5e173640a3e56d46f09d76f0574f2`) and `draco_wasm_wrapper.js`
    (`e8049906ef3f8f75d3456c22a3f31bfdfe5b5b5bd09ccdec613b9e9a49d554d8`).
  - Basis Universal v1_50_0_2 WebGL transcoder from
    https://github.com/BinomialLLC/basis_universal/tree/v1_50_0_2/webgl/transcoder/build: `basis_transcoder.wasm`
    (`6cf17dc889352c42e9acf8897107978d127005fe3386c36a0e3845e27967630a`) and `basis_transcoder.js`
    (`8478b5b6d6b74e7d3082b89f6417321d8d1dc0307f2b30d4484bb11b441696a1`, before the build's static-embind step).
  - jxl-oxide-wasm 0.12.6 from npm, https://www.npmjs.com/package/jxl-oxide-wasm/v/0.12.6 (checked 2026-11-06):
    `jxl_oxide_wasm_bg.wasm` (sha256 `3336f3abd4a04fccc437e7a84f12d4b63c12f302044110867f99be14c4c75a69`) and
    `jxl_oxide_wasm.js` (`d9a314abc55d167e94e2d995ce6ab5276f86ef9de41f06df11fef3acf55ff6b7`). The crates inside it are named in
    `dist/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICE.md`.
- **Siemens JT notice (`@margoengine/brep`, `@margoengine/cad`).** The JT reader in `packages/brep/src/jt` reads the
  format as described in the Siemens JT File Format Reference and ISO 14306 (`docs/jt-licensing.md`). Both packages'
  tracked `NOTICE` files ship in their tarballs with the reference licence terms, the royalty-free patent notice and the
  trademark note, and every JT reader source file carries the same notice in its header.
- **MPL-2.0 (web-ifc, peer of `@margoengine/ifc`).** Not redistributed in any tarball: the app installs it. A site or
  app that serves `web-ifc.wasm` must say where its source is (https://github.com/ThatOpen/engine_web-ifc).
- **Optional local tool, never shipped (sharp and libvips).** sharp (Apache-2.0) and its prebuilt libvips binaries
  (LGPL-3.0) are installed as an optional dependency of Next.js for `examples/next`, and
  `scripts/optimize-demo-assets.js` and `scripts/build-scifi-helmet.mjs` use sharp to resize textures. `margo-convert
  build` also uses a sharp that is already installed in the project it runs in (WebP, AVIF and JPEG encoding, resizing);
  it is not a dependency or peer of any package, nothing is downloaded, and without it `margo-convert` falls back to
  its own PNG writer. Neither sharp nor libvips is in any tarball or served by the site.
- **MIT (React).** Keep the copyright and permission notice: npm dependencies carry their own
  LICENSE files.
- **Site and demos.** The site build copies this file to `/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`, so the demos that bundle Draco,
  Basis carry these notices next to the asset credits below.

## Development and workspace tooling (never shipped)

`package-lock.json` holds 188 third-party entries (build tools, test tools, the examples' and apps' own
dependencies, platform-optional binaries). Licences: MIT 95, Apache-2.0 45, MPL-2.0 13, LGPL-3.0-or-later 10, MIT OR Apache-2.0 9, ISC 4, Apache-2.0 AND LGPL-3.0-or-later 3, BSD-3-Clause 3, BSD-2-Clause 2, 0BSD 1, Apache-2.0 AND LGPL-3.0-or-later AND MIT 1, CC-BY-4.0 1, MIT-0 1.
Install scripts anywhere in the lock: fsevents@2.3.3, webgpu@0.6.2. Deprecated: whatwg-encoding@3.1.1. `webgpu` is a development dependency only, for the Node proof of `@margoengine/headless`, and is never shipped; its
install script only clears the macOS quarantine flag on its binary. `rhino3dm` and `laz-perf` are not in the lock: the opt-in
`test:real-files:runtimes` tool of `@margoengine/loaders` fetches them at pinned versions into an ignored folder, for real-file tests only. CI and releases install with `npm ci`, which refuses a lockfile that does not match `package.json` and checks
every tarball against its integrity hash.
`aioquic` (BSD-3-Clause) is not in the lock: `packages/netcode/tests/webtransport-proof/server.py` uses it through a Python virtual environment of your own, for the by-hand WebTransport proof only. It is never shipped.

## Hemoglobin absorption spectra (materials skin, 2026-11-18)

packages/materials/src/skin-spectrum.ts holds the molar extinction coefficients of oxy- and deoxy-hemoglobin every 4 nm
from 380 to 780 nm, taken unchanged from Scott Prahl's "Tabulated Molar Extinction Coefficient for Hemoglobin in Water"
(Oregon Medical Laser Center, https://omlc.org/spectra/hemoglobin/summary.html, compiled from data of W. B. Gratzer and
N. Kollias), retrieved 2026-11-18. Measured physical data, used with attribution; the page states no licence terms. No
program code is included.

## Measured tennis-ball bounces (physics rigid validation, 2026-11-27)

packages/physics/tests/rigid-materials.test.js holds, as test data, measured values from R. Cross, "Measurements of the
horizontal coefficient of restitution for a superball and a tennis ball", American Journal of Physics 70(5), 482-489, 2002,
https://doi.org/10.1119/1.1450571 (author's copy, https://www.physics.usyd.edu.au/~cross/PUBLICATIONS/20.%20HorizCOR.PDF):
the ball's mass and radii, its restitution and its sliding friction on timber, Rebound Ace and emery (sections V and VI),
and from Table II each bounce's incidence angle, incoming speed, vx2 / vx1, rebound angle and time-average friction.
Measured physical data, used with attribution; the paper's text and figures are not copied. Never shipped (test data). No
program code is included.

## Measured domino wave speeds (physics rigid validation, 2026-11-27)

packages/physics/tests/rigid-measured.test.js holds, as test data, five wave speeds over sqrt(g H) against the spacing over
the height from R. Larham, "Validation of a Model of the Domino Effect?", arXiv:0803.2898, 2008, appendix A table 1,
https://arxiv.org/abs/0803.2898 (arXiv's non-exclusive distribution licence). Measured physical data, used with
attribution; the paper's text is not copied. Never shipped (test data). No program code is included.

## Measured leaf and flower spectra (scatter grass and procedural forbs, 2026-11-28)

Measured data copied with credit (Scott, 2026-11-28). No program code is included; only values derived from these files
ship (the default colours of `@margoengine/scatter/grass` and `@margoengine/procedural/forbs`), and the tests integrate
the files again.

- `packages/scatter/test/fixtures/leaf-spectra.json`: leaf reflectance and transmittance, 380 to 780 nm every 10 nm,
  means of sycamore maple leaves grouped by chlorophyll, from the ANGERS Leaf Optical Properties Database (2003), S.
  Jacquemoud, L. Bidel, C. Francois and G. Pavan, INRA Angers, distributed by EcoSIS (https://ecosis.org, package
  2231d4f6-981e-4408-bf23-1b2b303f475e) under its "Other (Open)" licence with this citation; described in Feret et
  al., Remote Sensing of Environment 112, 3030 (2008). Retrieved 2026-11-28.
- `packages/procedural/test/fixtures/forb-spectra.json`: petal and leaf reflectance of alpine forbs (Arnica montana,
  Gentiana acaulis and grandiflora, Aster alpinus, Bistorta vivipara, Silene acaulis and the leaves of eight alpine
  species), from FReD, the Floral Reflectance Database (S. E. J. Arnold, S. Faruq, V. Savolainen, P. W. McOwan and L.
  Chittka, PLoS ONE 5(12), e14287, 2010, http://www.reflectance.co.uk), open access with this citation; the records
  are from Chittka et al., Vision Research 34, 1489 (1994) and Chittka, J. Theor. Biol. 181, 179 (1996). Retrieved
  2026-11-28.

## Measured material data sets (materials library, 2026-11-28)

Scott, 2026-11-28: measured data sets may be copied with credit, each in its own data file under its own licence. The
materials library (packages/materials/src/measured.ts) ships only values derived from these files; the files sit in
packages/materials/test/fixtures, each with its source and licence in its `_header`. No program code is included.

- `optical-constants.json`: metal n and k tables and dielectric dispersion formulas from the refractiveindex.info
  database (M. N. Polyanskiy, "Refractiveindex.info database of optical constants", Scientific Data 11, 94, 2024,
  https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-023-02898-2, https://github.com/polyanskiy/refractiveindex.info-database), CC0 1.0.
  Each entry names the paper the database transcribes (Johnson and Christy 1972 and 1974, Rakic 1995, Werner et al.
  2009, Querry 1985 and 1987, Mathewson and Myers 1971, Inagaki et al. 1981, Palm et al. 2018, Karlsson and Ribbing
  1982, Malitson 1962 and 1965, Peter 1923, Ghosh 1999, Daimon and Masumura 2007, Warren and Brandt 2008, Rubin 1985,
  Sultanova et al. 2009, Sani and Dell'Oro 2016, Synowicki and Tiwald 2004). Retrieved 2026-11-28.
- `surface-spectra.json`: visible reflectance spectra resampled to 10 nm from the ECOSTRESS Spectral Library 1.0
  (S. K. Meerdink, S. J. Hook, D. A. Roberts and E. A. Abbott, Remote Sensing of Environment 230, 111196, 2019,
  https://speclib.jpl.nasa.gov) and its ASTER part (A. M. Baldridge et al., Remote Sensing of Environment 113, 711,
  2009), NASA JPL data, free to use with these citations; the gabbro row (black granite) is the JHU sample Gabbro_H1.
  Retrieved 2026-11-28.
- `physicallybased.json`: rows of the physically based materials database (A. Palmqvist, https://physicallybased.info,
  https://github.com/AntonPalmqvist/physically-based-api), CC0 1.0. Retrieved 2026-11-28.

None of the three is share-alike. The CIE illuminant data sets (CC BY-SA 4.0) are not used here.

## EGM96 geoid grid (`@margoengine/controls/geoid`)

`packages/controls/data/egm96-15.bin` (shipped in the controls package's dist when present) is the EGM96 15-minute geoid
undulation grid of the US National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA) and NASA, `WW15MGH.GRD` from NGA's EGM96
interpolation package (https://earth-info.nga.mil/, Office of Geomatics, EGM96), re-packed unchanged in value to
little-endian int16 centimetres (721 x 1441, 2,077,922 bytes) by `scripts/geoid/pack-egm96.mjs`. US Government work,
public domain; credit NGA and NASA, no endorsement. Reference: Lemoine et al., "The Development of the Joint NASA GSFC
and NIMA Geopotential Model EGM96", NASA/TP-1998-206861, 1998. Data only; no NGA interpolation code (INTPT.f) is read
or used. The committed file (2026-11-26, Scott approved the download) was packed from NGA's own `ww15mgh.grd.z`
(Unix compress) as NGA served it at
http://earth-info.nga.mil/GandG/wgs84/gravitymod/egm96/ww15mgh.grd.z, fetched from the Internet Archive's
2006-11-20 capture of that address
(https://web.archive.org/web/20061120214936id_/http://earth-info.nga.mil:80/GandG/wgs84/gravitymod/egm96/ww15mgh.grd.z),
because earth-info.nga.mil refused connections from the workstation. SHA-256: `ww15mgh.grd.z`
5b789d8c2a3163cc48f7d8f194ebe6fcbfcde8417ed687b8f113fe76d29508e9, unpacked `WW15MGH.GRD` (9,618,935 bytes)
c2537a9420a9398ee1e3d5e3506e14aafa47bed1cdc5c8f1a37cd18a209903a0, packed `egm96-15.bin`
e8114a8ae5eedc1e69d89ed1c5ea8e617bc70657ad95bf0633616d7bd15d04f0 (heights -106.991 m to 85.391 m).

## Dam-break measurements (water, GPULiquid checks, 2026-11-28)

packages/water/test/gpu-liquid-dambreak.test.js holds measured values copied unchanged, used with attribution:

- J. C. Martin and W. J. Moyce, "An experimental study of the collapse of liquid columns on a rigid horizontal plane",
  Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 244 (1952), 312-324, https://doi.org/10.1098/rsta.1952.0006 (read from the scan at
  https://www.math.ntu.edu.tw/~shyue/orch08/benchmarks/lowmach/broken-dam/91519.pdf): the runs' T at each Z of their
  tables 1 to 3 that the test uses (table 1 to Z = 13, table 2 to Z = 12, table 3 to Z = 7.67) and the normalising T
  at Z = 1.44. The paper states no licence for its tables.
- L. Lobovsky, E. Botia-Vera, F. Castellana, J. Mas-Soler and A. Souto-Iglesias, "Experimental investigation of
  dynamic pressure loads during dam break", J. Fluids Struct. 48 (2014), 407-434,
  https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jfluidstructs.2014.03.009 (arXiv:1308.0115, arXiv's non-exclusive distribution licence
  1.0): the front's mean speeds of their Table 1 (1.56 and 1.34 sqrt(g H) at 300 and 600 mm, and the 1.14 to 1.74 range
  of the dam breaks it gathers).

No program code is included.

## Human body measurement tables (`@margoengine/rigging/anatomy/human`)

Three published tables are held as data files, each with its source and licence at its top. They are typed copies of
published group values read on 2026-11-28; no file of another party is redistributed and no per-person data is held.

- packages/rigging/src/anatomy-data-cdc.ts: the reference values (means and 95% confidence intervals by sex and age
  group) of the CDC Normal Joint Range of Motion Study, from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention page
  https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/ncbddd/jointrom/index.html ; Soucie JM et al., "Range of motion measurements:
  reference values and a database for comparison studies", Haemophilia 17(3):500-507, 2011. A publication of a United
  States federal agency; the page prints no licence statement. The study's downloadable per-person dataset has its own
  data use restrictions and is not used.
- packages/rigging/src/anatomy-data-ansur2.ts: summary statistics (mean and standard deviation by sex) of 48
  dimensions of ANSUR II (lengths and heights, and since 2026-11-28 the limb girths and the chest and waist depths and
  breadths the pose checker sizes its body volumes from), from Gordon CC et al., "2012 Anthropometric Survey of U.S. Army Personnel: Methods and
  Summary Statistics", U.S. Army Natick Soldier Research, Development and Engineering Center, NATICK/TR-15/007, read
  from https://tools.openlab.psu.edu/publicData/ANSURII-TR15-007.pdf . Distribution statement of the report: "Approved
  for public release; distribution is unlimited". Credit: U.S. Army; no endorsement.
- packages/rigging/src/anatomy-data-deleva.ts: segment mass shares and centres of mass from table 4 of de Leva P,
  "Adjustments to Zatsiorsky-Seluyanov's segment inertia parameters", Journal of Biomechanics 29(9):1223-1230, 1996,
  https://doi.org/10.1016/0021-9290(95)00178-6 . The paper is copyright Elsevier; only the table's measured values are
  cited, with credit, and none of its text or figures.

[Article](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0022112005006105)

### BREAK-03 steel tube compression measurements

`packages/physics/scripts/break03-steel-tube-measured.mjs` contains specimen, tensile and experimental force scalars from Tables 1, 2 and 4 and sparse numerical readings from Figures 5 and 29. J. Y. Jung measured these specimens for *On the Collision Strength of Ship’s Bow* (1997), Pusan National University. Young Il Park, Jin-Seong Cho and Jeong-Hwan Kim republished the data in *Numerical and Experimental Investigation of Quasi-Static Crushing Behaviors of Steel Tubular Structures*, Materials 15, 2107 (2022), © 2022 the authors. The numeric conversions and production comparison are new. [Publication and data](https://doi.org/10.3390/ma15062107) · [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)

### MARINTEK rogue-wave flume comparison (SEA-03)

`packages/physics/scripts/sea03-flume-crests-measured.mjs` transcribes three published gauge crest counts, threshold definitions and wavemaker settings separately from Dematteis, Grafke, Onorato and Vanden-Eijnden, [Experimental Evidence of Hydrodynamic Instantons: The Universal Route to Rogue Waves](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevX.9.041057), Physical Review X 9, 041057, published in 2019 by the American Physical Society. The authors released the paper under [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). No raw recordings or figures are included.

### Boers barred beach measurements (SEA-05)

`packages/physics/scripts/sea05-boers-measured.mjs` records sparse physical bed coordinates and actual Boers flume wave-height and water-level markers. The observation markers and separate offshore height and period are adapted with metric rounding and datum adjustment from figure 10 and Table 3 of [Moghimi et al. 2020](https://doi.org/10.3390/jmse8050308), licensed [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). The physical bed facts come from figure 2 of [Daly et al. 2012](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.coastaleng.2011.08.001). The original figures and time series are outside the repository.

### Lake Superior November 1975 forcing and observations (SEA-07)

`packages/physics/scripts/sea07-superior-measured.mjs` retrieves published [NOAA CO-OPS gauge observations](https://api.tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/api/dev/) and the [NOAA NCEI Great Lakes bathymetry](https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/products/great-lakes-bathymetry). Atmospheric forcing is adapted from [Copernicus Climate Change Service and ECMWF ERA5](https://doi.org/10.24381/cds.adbb2d47), [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/), accessed through [Open-Meteo](https://open-meteo.com/en/docs/historical-weather-api). The script resamples the independent forcing onto the model grid. Downloaded inputs are kept in its local cache.

### ATMO-04 measured precipitation

- Gires, Tchiguirinskaia and Schertzer, *Two months of disdrometer data in the Paris area* (2018), data archive [10.5281/zenodo.1240168](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.1240168), CC BY 4.0. The diagnostic reads synchronized PWS100 forcing and independently observed Parsivel2 size and speed bins.
- Kuhn and Vázquez-Martín, *Dual Ice Crystal Imager (D-ICI) data*, version 1 (2021), [10.5878/dgak-p185](https://doi.org/10.5878/dgak-p185), CC BY 4.0. The diagnostic reads the 94 explicit aggregate records and applies the published instrument allowance.
- Locatelli and Hobbs (1974), [Fall speeds and masses of solid precipitation particles](https://doi.org/10.1029/JC079i015p02185). The diagnostic transcribes sparse observed Fig. 20 coordinates and notes their overlapping model lineage. The archive payloads are downloaded separately.

### ICE-04 measured towing resistance

Yanzhuo Xue, Kai Zhong, Bao-Yu Ni, Zhiyuan Li, Martin Bergström, Jonas W. Ringsberg and Luofeng Huang (2024), [Ocean Engineering 292, 116476](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.oceaneng.2023.116476), CC BY 4.0. The diagnostic transcribes four measured model-tow resistance values and their repeated-trial uncertainty in Table 3. Geometry, floe properties and measured friction come from the experimental setup. The diagnostic implements the comparison in Margo.

### ICE-01 Col de Porte snowpack observations

Samuel Morin, Yves Lejeune, Bernard Lesaffre, Jean-Michel Panel, Daniel Poncet, Pierre David and Marcel Sudul (2012), [Col de Porte meteorology and snow measurements](https://doi.org/10.1594/PANGAEA.774249), CC BY 3.0. The diagnostic separately downloads the hourly forcing, hourly snow depth and daily snow water equivalent. It reads initialization values once and uses later observations only for comparison. [Dataset paper](https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-4-13-2012)

### ICE-03 measured capsize

- Burton et al. (2012), [Laboratory investigations of iceberg capsize dynamics](https://doi.org/10.1029/2011JF002055). The diagnostic uses sparse factual readings from Figure 5. The [archived measurements](https://doi.org/10.7265/N56H4FCJ) carry CC BY-NC 4.0 and are referenced separately.
- Heller et al. (2019), [Large-scale experiments into the tsunamigenic potential of different iceberg calving mechanisms](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-018-36634-3), CC BY 4.0. The motion file is supplied externally from the authors' [SPHERIC Test 15](https://www.spheric-sph.org/tests/test-15). The engine bundles neither archive.

### AERO-05 samara measurements

`packages/physics/scripts/aero05-samara-measured.mjs` transcribes a small set of Norway maple morphology and
still-air laboratory descent and spin statistics from Table 1 of Gary K. Nave Jr., Nathaniel Hall, Katrina Somers,
Brock Davis, Hope Gruszewski, Craig Powers, Michael Collver, David G. Schmale III and Shane D. Ross,
[*Wind Dispersal of Natural and Biomimetic Maple Samaras*](https://doi.org/10.3390/biomimetics6020023),
Biomimetics 6(2), 23 (2021), [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).
The script converts to SI and derives representative planform area from mean wing loading. Original figures, video,
models and raw records are not included.

### EARTH-05 soil measurements

`packages/physics/scripts/earth05-plates-measured.mjs` uses sparse derived measurements from
[Apfelbeck et al. (2011), Fig. 8](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jterra.2011.04.001) and
[Rashidi and Gholami (2011), Fig. 7](https://www.arpnjournals.com/jabs/research_papers/rp_2011/jabs_0311_255.pdf).
The cited papers retain their copyrights. The script contains factual readouts and a separate
circular material calibration. It includes no original plots or experimental files.

### EARTH-08 Mashiki measurements

`packages/physics/scripts/earth08-mashiki-measured.mjs` uses the original P–S logging layer
values from [NIED KiK-net KMMH16](https://doi.org/10.17598/NIED.0004) as reproduced in
[NILIM and PWRI (2023), Fig. 4.34](https://www.nilim.go.jp/lab/bcg/siryou/tnn/tnn1247pdf/ks1247.pdf),
and separate weak-motion readouts from [Esfahani et al. (2024), Fig. 2 and §3.1](https://doi.org/10.1093/gji/ggae222).
No waveform archives, original plots or implementation code are included.

### ICE-05 channel-freezing observations

Bouke Johannes Kaaks, Danny Lathouwers, Jan-Leen Kloosterman and Martin Rohde (2025),
[*Transient freezing of water in a square channel: An experimental investigation*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.expthermflusci.2025.111417),
[CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). The ICE-05 diagnostic converts the reported
temperature fits to kelvin and transcribes sparse cold-plate observations and uncertainty in SI.
No plots, full datasets or source code are bundled.

### FIRE-06 gallium melt-front observations

C. Gau and R. Viskanta (1986), [*Melting and Solidification of a Pure Metal on a Vertical Wall*](https://doi.org/10.1115/1.3246884),
Fig. 2(a), supplies nine sparse SI distances transcribed from the experimental trace reproduced by S. Meyer
(2016), [*A Fluid Dynamics Approach for Solid-Liquid Phase Change in Binary and Elemental Melts*](https://publikationen.bibliothek.kit.edu/1000058183/3880102),
Fig. 5.8. The diagnostic bundles those reported facts and the independently tabulated material constants.

### SOUND-04 simply supported plate observations

Patrick Dumond, Dominic Monette, Fadi Alladkani, James Akl and Inès Chikhaoui (2019),
[*Simplified setup for the vibration study of plates with simply-supported boundary conditions*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mex.2019.09.023),
[CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). The diagnostic transcribes only the
dimensions and mode readings for plates 1 and 4 and nominal material inputs from Tables 3–5,
converting quantities to SI.

### BIO-02 red maple shade-tent observations

Kurt W. Gottschalk (1985), [*Effects of shading on growth and development of northern red oak, black oak,
black cherry, and red maple seedlings. I. Height, diameter, and root/shoot ratio*](https://research.fs.usda.gov/treesearch/47682),
USDA Forest Service research presented at the Fifth Central Hardwood Forest Conference.
The diagnostic includes only the reported treatment light fractions and sparse red maple height means from
Tables 2 and 4.

### BIO-03 measured Douglas-fir survival

Robert A. Slesak, Michelle C. Agne, Constance A. Harrington and Matthew D. Powers (2025),
[*Long-term effects of tree spacing during reforestation on survival and growth of three important tree species
in the Pacific Northwest, USA*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.foreco.2025.122724), §3.1 and Fig. 1c.
The diagnostic transcribes sparse survival means and reported intervals. Independent plot layout facts are
from Robert O. Curtis, Sheel Bansal and Constance A. Harrington (2016),
[USDA Forest Service PNW-RP-607](https://pubs.usgs.gov/publication/70173842).

### BIO-04 atmospheric corrosion coupon observations

Rosa Vera et al. (2022), [*Corrosion Behavior of Copper Exposed in Marine Tropical Atmosphere in Rapa Nui
(Easter Island) Chile 20 Years after MICAT*](https://doi.org/10.3390/met12122082), and Luca Paterlini et al.
(2024), [*Atmospheric Corrosion of Different Steel Types in Urban and Marine Exposure*](https://doi.org/10.3390/ma17246211),
[CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). The diagnostic converts a few reported deposition,
ambient climate and penetration values to solver units. It includes no figures or source code.

### LIFE-01 measured treadmill cohort statistics

A. I. Gmel, E. H. Haraldsdóttir, F. M. Serra Bragança, A. M. Cruz and M. A. Weishaupt (2024),
[*Comparison of speed-dependent time, force and spatial parameters between Franches-Montagnes and European Warmblood horses walking and trotting on a treadmill*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jevs.2024.105005), Journal of Equine Veterinary Science 133, 105005. [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). The diagnostic transcribes sparse cohort metadata and measured means and deviations from Tables 1, 2 and 4. It converts units and includes no original figure or trial dataset.

### AERO-02 flume diagnostic data

`packages/physics/scripts/aero02-sail-measured.mjs` includes camber section samples derived from the zero-twist specimen in Abel Arredondo Galeana and Ignazio Maria Viola’s [PIV dataset for near wake of spinnaker (2020)](https://doi.org/10.7488/ds/2857), University of Edinburgh, [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). The archived solid was reduced to a sampled midsurface with dimensions rounded to 0.01 mm. The script identifies the archive member and checksum. Held-out force coefficients transcribe five Figure 4(a) readings from Abel Arredondo-Galeana, Holger Babinsky and Ignazio Maria Viola, [Vortex Flow of Downwind Sails (2023)](https://doi.org/10.1017/flo.2023.1), also CC BY 4.0. This repository contains the derived numbers and source references.
